Note::NlpAccessor::mask_dates¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::NlpAccessor::mask_dates() const

Replace Date-Shaped Spans Without Rewriting The Record¶

mask_dates() replaces recognized calendar expressions with [DATE]. Choose it when downstream work needs to know that a date occurred but must not retain its exact value. It does not alter standalone years, times, or arbitrary numbers.

Family

Accepted shape

Examples

Year first

YYYY-MM-DD, with -, /, or . used consistently

2024-01-02

Month first

MM/DD/YY or MM/DD/YYYY

12/31/2024

Day first

DD.MM.YY or DD.MM.YYYY

31.12.2024

Named month

English month name, day, optional year

January 2, 2024, Sep 7

Numeric month fields are restricted to 1 through 12 and day fields to 1 through 31. Mixed separators such as 2024-01/02 do not match. The operation is intentionally a conservative text recognizer, not a civil-calendar parser: Feb 31, 2024 is date-shaped and is masked. This avoids leaking a date-like identifier merely because its source is malformed. Use Timeline construction when calendar validity is the question.

Matches are case-insensitive for English month names. Relative language such as tomorrow, day-first named forms such as 2 January 2024, and non-English month names are outside this method’s grammar. [DATE] itself is unchanged on another pass.

Shape And Failure Contract¶

The operation accepts only Text Notes, allocates a fresh packed Text result, and preserves scalar, vector, matrix, or rank-three shape exactly. Undefined input remains undefined. Empty input remains a defined empty Note. Bytes and native dtypes reject before scanning.

Example 1: Every Accepted Family¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"2024-01-02", "12/31/2024", "31.12.2024",
                       "January 2, 2024", "Sep 7"})
        .nlp().mask_dates()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[5], dim=1, numel=5, encoding=utf8)
["[DATE]", "[DATE]", "[DATE]", "[DATE]", "[DATE]"]

Example 2: Range And Separator Boundaries¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({
        "keep 2024-13-01 and 2024-01/02; syntax Feb 31, 2024"})
        .nlp().mask_dates()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["keep 2024-13-01 and 2024-01/02; syntax [DATE]"]

Example 3: Empty, Undefined, And Bytes¶

const auto empty = pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::string>{})
                       .nlp().mask_dates();
std::cout << "dates empty dim=" << empty.dim()
          << " numel=" << empty.numel() << '\n';
std::cout << "dates undefined=" << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().nlp().mask_dates().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::bytes(
      std::vector<std::string>{"2024-01-02"},
      std::array<std::int64_t, 1>{1}).nlp().mask_dates();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "dates Bytes: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

dates empty dim=1 numel=0
dates undefined=false
dates Bytes: rejected

  • mask_pii: apply date masking with the other sensitive categories.
